evidence: git init --bare without -b main on a host with init.defaultBranch unset leaves the fixture remote's HEAD at a never-pushed master; git clone warns 'remote HEAD refers to nonexistent ref, unable to checkout' and lands unborn (reproduced by hand on git 2.43.0)
unmodified suite at c1701be: 4/14 red with init.defaultBranch unset or =master; 14/14 green with =main (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL override, nothing else changed)
git rev-parse HEAD on an unborn HEAD: rc=128, stdout 'HEAD' — the string the old guard compared against a commit
in the fixture main is published, hence never bundled, hence resume never touches HEAD: the 5 restored refs are unrelated to HEAD
the divergence control's commit onto unborn master created a new root, so the identity gate fired before the refusal under test

DEFAULTS_TAKEN.condition: The dispatch places me in the shared root checkout on main with peers editing concurrently; a branch switch in the root is reserved (§21d) and a task branch would need a worktree I was not given.
DEFAULTS_TAKEN.default: Committed on main directly from the root through scripts/legend_commit.sh, path-scoped to my five files, as §21e item 1 permits for a change finished when written.
DEFAULTS_TAKEN.why_safe: The commit is path-scoped and lock-serialised; no peer file can be swept in; main is writable by every actor (§21e SURFACES).
DEFAULTS_TAKEN.what_would_have_been_different: A task branch would have had to be landed the same day by task_close.py; the result on main is identical.

DEFAULTS_TAKEN.condition: The finding hypothesised that resume leaves HEAD unborn after restoring refs; the fixture showed HEAD was unborn before resume ran.
DEFAULTS_TAKEN.default: Recorded the hypothesis as false-as-stated in the Resolution without rewriting the diagnosis above it; still delivered the case the finding asked for (HEAD asserted where the bundle says) because the landing code path is real even though the fixture's four reds did not exercise it.
DEFAULTS_TAKEN.why_safe: The evidence is reproducible in one command (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL override); the case costs nothing and closes a path a future host could hit.
DEFAULTS_TAKEN.what_would_have_been_different: Trusting the finding would have produced a fix to a landing that was never reached, and left the fixture host-dependent.

DEFAULTS_TAKEN.condition: Whether an unborn destination should be populated when the bundle carries the checked-out branch, or refused outright (the protocol prefers declared limitations over widening).
DEFAULTS_TAKEN.default: Land it — a fast-forward from nothing discards nothing — and refuse by name when the bundle does not carry the branch. Recorded as limitation 10.
DEFAULTS_TAKEN.why_safe: Both branches are mutation-tested (M2, M3); the divergence control proves work is still never discarded; the only new behaviour is on a destination that has no work at all.
DEFAULTS_TAKEN.what_would_have_been_different: A pure refusal would have been simpler but would leave a `git init -b main` + fetch bootstrap (what reconstruct_real builds before its reset) unable to receive dirty patches.

DEFAULTS_TAKEN.why_safe: The dispatch's ownership rule; the red is attributable by timestamp and by file.
